title: Headcount gating decision ladder and price sensitivity cheatsheet
content:
Purpose: quick operational playbook for aligning short-term hiring decisions with token-price moves and runway signals. Intended as a lightweight reference for finance, recruiting, and eng-rpm during volatile demand windows.

High-level thesis and constraints:
- We prefer discrete gating steps tied to observable signals rather than continuous manual tactics.
- Hiring is the slowest lever (lag 6–12 weeks). Pricing and commit gating are the fastest.
- Preserve a 12–16 week runway cushion for critical platform roles (SRE, serving runtime, infra); feature and GTM roles have more flexible tolerance.

Key baseline metrics (internal quick-check numbers, approximate):
- Current net burn (cash) = $3.2M / month.
- Active headcount = 148 FTEs.
- Average fully-loaded monthly comp per hire = $18k (eng leads higher, interns lower).
- Token mix: 60% generation, 30% embeddings, 10% eval/rerank.
- Effective cost per 1M tokens served = $65 (weighted across fleet + amortized infra).

Signals we care about (priority order):
1) Token demand delta (7-day moving avg vs prior 30d): sustained +20% -> escalate.
2) Unit cost creep (fleet cost / M tokens) > +8% MOM -> investigate.
3) Take rate vs committed capacity > 85% for 7 days -> capacity risk.
4) Revenue recognition changes / major renewals slipping -> revenue risk.
5) Customer SLA incidents impacting margin -> reliability risk.

Gating ladder (actionable steps tied to signals):
- Tier 0 (Green): signals within +/-5% of baseline. Actions: proceed with planned hires; no pricing changes; maintain normal sourcing cadence.
- Tier 1 (Amber): any signal crosses amber threshold (e.g., demand +15–30%, unit cost +5–8%). Actions (fast): enable 72-hour pricing nudge on non-enterprise routes (+3–5% effective); postpone non-critical job offers (soft freeze); enable burst reserve credits for top 10 customers. Actions (medium): accelerate autoscaling config review, tighten caching TTLs.
- Tier 2 (Red): sustained signals >30% demand growth or unit cost >+12% or take rate >95%. Actions (fast): institute temporary 10–15% price uplift on new signups and non-committed traffic; pause non-critical hiring (freeze new reqs); engage sales to convert high-volume customers to committed plans; trigger emergency SRE-on-call capacity. Actions (medium): open dedicated procurement for GPU spot pool expansion; evaluate short-term contract hires for ops.
- Tier 3 (Critical): multiple signals + revenue realization below runway trigger (runway <10w). Actions: emergency exec review; prioritize survival hires only (SRE, customers at risk); consider limited feature rollback or temporary throughput throttles; start formal contingency planning for burn reduction.

Pricing sensitivity quick matrix (illustrative):
- Scenario A (Price -10%): volume increases +25% in 90 days, gross margin falls by ~9ppt if cost per token unchanged -> net burn up. Hiring recommendation: defer senior non-critical hires; increase monitoring cadence.
- Scenario B (Price flat): volume +8% -> manageable. Hiring: proceed with 25% of planned hires this quarter, defer remainder to next hiring window.
- Scenario C (Price +8%): volume -6% -> margin improves ~5ppt, runway +6 weeks. Hiring: green-light 60% of planned hires; prioritize mid-senior engineers.

How we translate price deltas to hiring gates (rule-of-thumb):
- For each 5% sustained drop in effective price, reduce planned hires by 10–15% (weighted towards non-core functions).
- For each 5% sustained increase, consider accelerating hires by 5–10% if pipeline velocity and candidate lead times justify.

Hiring priority buckets (shortlist for freeze/proceed decisions):
1) Critical (never freeze unless Tier 3): SRE, serving runtime, security, core infra.
2) High (evaluate case-by-case): model ops, platform performance, dedicated account engineering for committed customers.
3) Medium (first to pause): product teams not on guaranteed revenue paths, growth marketing.
4) Low (easy to pause): contractors, new grad cohorts, exploratory research hiring.

Quick cash-forward sensitivity (ballpark math):
- One senior engineer hire (fully-loaded) = $18k/mo. Pausing 10 hires for 3 months -> cash saved ~ $540k.
- Small price uplift +8% on on-demand routes: incremental margin capture ~ $220–420k/month depending on elasticity.
- Constrained GPU spot expansion (procure extra 12% spot capacity) costs ~ $120k/month but reduces unit cost variance.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Produce 2-pg exec summary with 3 scenarios (cash / hires / pricing) for next CFO sync (owner: Daniel).
- Validate elasticity assumptions with growth analytics: estimate cross-route elasticity by cohort (owner: Priya).
- Connect with recruiting on candidate pipeline lead times by role (owner: Marcus).

Notes to self / working hypotheses:
- We should avoid knee-jerk company-wide hiring freezes; instead use tiered freezes that preserve critical runway for ops.
- Pricing nudges are high-leverage and reversible; use them before hitting hiring freezes when possible.
- Communicate gating thresholds clearly to product and sales so they can prioritize conversion/commits.

Slack refs: #finance-runway, #eng-capacity. Confluence: price-sensitivity model (linked above).

Revision log:
- 2026-04-02: initial draft (Sophia)

- 2026-04-12: clarified hiring buckets and open actions (Priya)

End of cheatsheet.
